 Follow Cheddar cheese sold in 12 states recalled. See impacted products
 Julia Gomez, USA TODAY Updated Wed, November 11, 2026 at 3:22 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Cheddar cheese products sold in 12 states are being recalled due to possible listeria contamination.
 Family Farmstead Dairy is recalling all of its raw cheddar cheese products with expiration dates on or before Oct. 16, 2027, due to possible contamination, according to a recall notice posted by the Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
 "Family Farmstead Dairy appreciates the cooperation of its distributors, retailers, and customers and apologizes for any inconvenience this action may cause," the company said in the recall announcement. "The company remains committed to producing safe, high-quality dairy products and maintaining the trust of the communities it serves."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The cheese was sold and distributed to retail stores in 12 states, including New York, New Jersey, Tennessee and others.
 Consumer Reports , the nonprofit known for testing and monitoring consumer-facing policy and products, released its annual risky food report in April, naming the 10 foods of 2024 that were subject to the most recalls and/or associated with the largest illness outbreaks. USA TODAY broke it down further on a what-you-need-to-know basis. 
 (Joe Raedle, Getty Images) Deli meat is somewhat of a "risky" food as it is often associated with the spread of listeria, such as in the 2024 case of the Boar's Head listeria outbreak that killed 10. Listeria monocytogenes is a hardy germ that can survive in very low temperatures but thrives in cool and damp places. It can, and will, happily live on foods in your or your grocery store's storage area, and the process for mass-producing the meat lends itself to plenty of opportunities for contamination.
 (Lauri Patterson, Getty Images) Produce, like the cucumbers recalled due to a salmonella  outbreak that infected 113 people across 23 states, can become adulterated with harmful bacteria through fecal contamination, which can occur through wastewater, water in the growing area, fertilizer and the proximity of the growing area to livestock.
 (Getty Images) Raw dairy, which is always unsafe to consume and illegal to sell in some states, poses a risk when it's not pasteurized. Dairy pasteurization, or heating milk products to a high enough temperature to kill harmful bacteria, has been practiced since the 1920s. (RA Simon, Getty Images) Cotija and queso fresco cheese are made from unpasteurized milk, meaning they carry an increased risk. One producer, Rizo-Lopez Foods, was shut down in October 2024 after its cheeses were linked to a years-long listeria outbreak that killed two people and made dozens of others sick.
 (Marcos Elihu Castillo Ramirez, Getty Images) Eggs can become contaminated via the same means as cucumbers and other raw produce, especially if they have a cracked shell. 
 (Getty Images) Like other raw produce, onions can become infected via fecal contamination. In 2024, E. coli-contaminated slivered onions on McDonald's Quarter Pounders triggered some locations to stop serving the burger temporarily. 
 (iStockphoto, Getty Images) Like cucumbers and onions, leafy greens are easily contaminated with bacteria like E. coli, as in the case of the Solata Foods spinach recall in 2024. 
 (Edalin, Getty Images) Organic carrots were linked to a major E. coli outbreak in late 2024, leaving at least 39 ill and one dead. 
 (Hyrma, Getty Images) Ready-to-eat/cooked poultry and meat have been the source of multiple major recalls and foodborne illness outbreaks in recent years. The same issue arises with RTE foods as with deli meat; the conditions they are made and stored under are often ideal for bacteria such as listeria to grow. In 2024, millions of pounds of RTE foods were recalled by BrucePac for listeria contamination. 
 (Getty Images) See the 'risky foods' linked to US recalls and illness outbreaks
 1 of 10 Consumer Reports , the nonprofit known for testing and monitoring consumer-facing policy and products, released its annual risky food report in April, naming the 10 foods of 2024 that were subject to the most recalls and/or associated with the largest illness outbreaks. USA TODAY broke it down further on a what-you-need-to-know basis. 
 (Joe Raedle, Getty Images) Listeria could cause serious infections, which can sometimes be fatal, especially in pregnant or elderly people, newborns and people with weakened immune systems.
 The recall announcement does not state whether any illnesses or incidents linked to the possible contamination were reported, nor does it list which retailers sold the recalled cheese. USA TODAY has contacted Family Farmstead Dairy for more information.
 The recall comes nearly a month after the company previously recalled raw cheddar products because they may have been contaminated with two strains of E. coli, USA TODAY previously reported .
 Advertisement Advertisement Here's what to know.
 Which products are being recalled?
 The following products are included in the recall, according to the FDA notice:
 8oz, plastic-wrapped Raw Mild Cheddar
 8oz, plastic-wrapped Raw Sharp Cheddar
 All lot codes that have a best-by date on or before Oct. 16, 2027, are included in the recall. No other products are included in the November recall.
 Family Farmstead Dairy recalled all of its cheddar products that have expiration dates on or before Oct. 16, 2027. Where was the recalled cheese sold?
 The recalled products were distributed in the following states:
 Connecticut
 Delaware
 Massachusetts
 New Hampshire
 New Jersey
 New York
 Pennsylvania
 Rhode Island
 Tennessee
 Vermont
 Virginia
 West Virginia
 Can't see the map? Click here . 
 Family Farmstead Dairy's previous recall
 On Oct. 15, the FDA posted an earlier recall announcement warning consumers that the company's cheese could have been contaminated with two strains of E. coli, USA TODAY previously reported. 
 Advertisement Advertisement The cheese was distributed to grocery stores in New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Connecticut, Maryland, Virginia and Massachusetts. However, the recalled cheese could have been distributed to stores in other states through distributors.
 The October recall included Family Farmstead Dairy Raw Mild Cheddar Cheese with the lot code 7/22/27 and a best-by date of July 22, 2027.
 No illnesses or reactions were reported related to the recall.
 What should consumers do if they purchased any of the recalled products?
 People who bought any of the recalled products should not consume them and can return them to the place of purchase for a refund.
 Anyone who has questions or requires additional assistance can email Family Farmstead Dairy at customerservice@familyfarmsteaddairy.com or call the company at 607-397-4044
 What are the symptoms of listeria infection?
 According to the recall notice, symptoms of listeria may include:
 Advertisement Advertisement High fever
 Severe headache
 Stiffness
 Nausea
 Abdominal pain
 Diarrhea
 Healthy people may experience only short-term illness, but listeria can cause serious infections in vulnerable groups.
 Who is most at risk?
 People at the highest risk of severe illness include:
 Pregnant people and their unborn or newborn babies
 Adults 65 and older
 People with weakened immune systems, including transplant recipients and people with conditions such as HIV/AIDS, cancer, diabetes and autoimmune diseases
 Listeria infections during pregnancy can result in miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery or life-threatening infections in newborns.
 What is raw milk cheese?
 Raw milk cheese is made from milk that has not been pasteurized, a heating process that kills many disease-causing germs. Raw milk products can carry harmful bacteria, and the FDA recommends choosing pasteurized dairy products to reduce the risk of foodborne illness.
